title: Hassockey / Jamaica Meadows
summary: Hassockey is a name preserved in early Jamaica records for marshy meadow localities. Because the records describe more than one tract, the marker is intentionally approximate.
address_label: General Jamaica / South Jamaica marsh landscape, Queens, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Representative point for multiple early Jamaica marsh and meadow localities; deliberately approximate.
why_this_matters: Hassockey keeps early Jamaica wetland geography visible in a landscape heavily altered by drainage and development. Its plural documentary use also shows why a historical place name may need a broad marker rather than a false single-site precision.
introduction_content: Hassockey appears in Jamaica-area records connected with marshy tracts of land. Recorded forms include Hassokie meadows, Hassokey swamp, and Hassokey Meadow.
translation_content: Tooker compared Hassockey with marsh-place vocabulary including Narragansett hassucki and Delaware assisku. The resemblance should be read as a historical linguistic interpretation rather than a settled modern translation.
land_loss_content: The Jamaica Hassockey records preserve how wet meadows, swamps, and marsh edges were named and managed in early town records. Keeping this as an unmapped draft prevents a false exact location while preserving the references for further review.
whereintheworld_content: The marker represents the general Jamaica and South Jamaica marsh landscape. The surviving records refer to multiple meadow or swamp localities and do not identify one modern parcel.
